title: The Attack Surface of Security Language

slides.title: The Attack Surface of Security Language
slides.body: Your security controls run on vocabulary. Who owns the definitions?
slides.source: post title; hook distilled from §intro + §Who Defines Normal
slides.exec_caption: The word becomes executable: if user dot trusted, allow.

slides.label: The premise
slides.headline: Security tooling is sold as if it were about attackers.
slides.body: Most of the time, it is about ordinary lives.
list: The volunteer locked out of a shared account
The user who does not resemble the model's idea of a person
slides.coda: The system does not ask who they are. It asks whether they fit.

slides.label: Detection is not perception
slides.definition: A distance from a chosen baseline.
slides.body: Every baseline encodes a population it considers ordinary. Whoever falls outside it pays in friction: repeated challenges and lost time, until the tool gets abandoned.
slides.source: post lines 33–37; strike renders the author's line 35 ('An anomaly is not a threat') as a diff

slides.label: Labels compress
slides.definition: Trust granted by someone, for a purpose, within a scope, under conditions that can change.
slides.body: The adjective hides every one of those clauses. That compression is an operational risk.
slides.source: post lines 51–57; strike renders line 55 ('compresses all of that into a character judgment')

slides.label: One word, three states
slides.body: Collapse them into one word and you create gaps an attacker can use and an operator may not notice until after the incident.

slides.label: The fix: a load-bearing lexicon
slides.headline: If changing a word's definition would alter an alert, permission, workflow, escalation path, or user consequence, govern it like code.

slides.label: The frameworks already admit context
items: describes AI systems as inherently socio-technical, shaped by human behavior and social dynamics.
places GOVERN at the center of its functions, starting with organizational context.
slides.body: The next step is to ask what that admission requires of the categories those systems use.
slides.source: post line 41; corroborated against airc.nist.gov AI RMF and NIST.CSWP.29 (2026-10-30)

slides.label: The human cost
slides.headline: A false positive leaves a social residue.
list: Users learn the system's idea of legitimate excludes them
The alert stream becomes a second inbox
slides.coda: Measure friction alongside detection. After every block, ask what behavior the system produced.

slides.label: Categories must remain repairable
slides.callout: The moment a word becomes load-bearing, it becomes part of the attack surface.
